questions.title: Testing a proposed clade
questions.stem:
Aligned sequences from three ingroup taxa and an outgroup have the six variable sites shown. For this question the outgroup bases are taken as ancestral. Each column represents a different position.

| Taxon | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Outgroup | A | C | G | T | A | C |
| R | G | T | G | T | G | C |
| S | G | T | A | T | A | C |
| T | A | C | G | C | A | T |

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Identify two shared derived characters supporting an R–S clade.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Calculate the observed R–S and R–T distances as numbers of differing sites. State why these figures are not estimates of genome-wide percentage divergence.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: A second gene supports an S–T group. Give two biological or sampling reasons for the conflict and an appropriate next step.

steps.text: Both R and S have G instead of ancestral A at site 1.
Both have T instead of ancestral C at site 2.
R and S differ at sites 3 and 5, so the distance is two.
R and T differ at sites 1, 2, 4, 5 and 6, so the distance is five.
The table deliberately includes only six variable positions and omits invariant sites.
Chance sampling of a short sequence or repeated mutation can mislead.
Different gene histories, for example introgression or incomplete lineage sorting, may differ from the species history; accept another distinct valid explanation.
Compare multiple independent loci with broader sampling before revising the species tree.

questions.answerSummary: Both R and S have G instead of ancestral A at site 1.

questions.title: Filament overlap during contraction
questions.stem:
Electron micrographs of comparable human sarcomeres were taken before and after stimulation. All lengths are in µm. The I-band measure in the table is the combined light-region width within one sarcomere.

| State | Z-to-Z distance | A band | Combined I regions |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Before | 2.50 | 1.60 | 0.90 |
| After | 2.05 | 1.60 | 0.45 |

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Calculate percentage shortening of the sarcomere and the percentage change in its combined I-region width.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Explain how the data support sliding filaments.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: A student observes a contracted fibre after ATP supply stops and concludes ATP is unnecessary. Evaluate that inference.

steps.text: Sarcomere shortening=(2.50−2.05)/2.50×100=18%.
The I regions decrease by 0.45/0.90×100=50%.
The smaller I regions account for the measured 0.45 µm reduction in total length.
A-band length is unchanged, consistent with constant thick-filament length.
Thin filaments slide past thick filaments, increasing overlap.
Z lines are pulled closer and the regions containing only thin filaments shrink.
Myosin heads can remain attached to actin when ATP is unavailable.
ATP binding is needed for detachment and hydrolysis helps reset the head for repeated cycling.
A static contracted state does not demonstrate continued ATP-independent cycling.

questions.answerSummary: Sarcomere shortening=(2.50−2.05)/2.50×100=18%.

questions.title: Interpreting light and carbon dioxide responses
questions.stem:
Net CO₂ uptake was measured on attached leaves under controlled conditions. Each value is the mean of six different plants. Units are µmol CO₂ m⁻² s⁻¹. Light intensities are in µmol photons m⁻² s⁻¹.

| Light intensity | 100 | 300 | 600 | 900 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| At 400 ppm CO₂ | 3 | 8 | 11 | 11 |
| At 800 ppm CO₂ | 3 | 10 | 17 | 19 |

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: At light intensity 600 calculate the percentage increase on raising CO₂ and compare it with the change at intensity 100.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Interpret the different responses using limiting factors.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Explain why an identical pair of means at intensity 100 does not prove a precisely zero effect, and identify two controls or data needed for a stronger comparison.

steps.text: At 600 the increase is 17−11=6 units.
Percentage increase=6/11×100≈54.5%.
At 100 both means are 3, so there is no observed increase.
At low intensity light delivery can limit ATP and reduced NADP production.
At 400 ppm, uptake plateaus between 600 and 900 even as light increases.
Additional CO₂ increases uptake at high light, supporting a CO₂ limitation under those conditions.
Means alone omit sampling variation and measurement uncertainty.
Report spread or confidence intervals for independent plants (or test the difference appropriately).
Control leaf temperature or another relevant factor such as humidity, leaf age or water availability.

questions.answerSummary: At 600 the increase is 17−11=6 units.

questions.title: Separating transcription and RNA stability
questions.stem:
A hormone is added to cultured cells. Total mature mRNA for gene X and newly synthesized RNA during an equal short pulse are measured relative to untreated samples. After the hormone treatment, transcription is stopped and the fraction of initial mature mRNA remaining is recorded.

| Treatment | New RNA in pulse | Mature mRNA at steady state | Fraction remaining after 2 h |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| No hormone | 1.0 | 1.0 | 0.50 |
| Hormone | 2.0 | 4.0 | 0.71 |

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Compare the two RNA measurements before transcription is stopped. Why is transcription alone an incomplete explanation if degradation conditions were unchanged?

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Assume exponential decay. Estimate the half-life in each treatment using the observation that 0.71²≈0.50.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Evaluate a claim that the hormone directly binds the promoter of gene X. Give one experiment that distinguishes direct promoter regulation from an indirect response.

steps.text: New RNA doubles while steady-state mature RNA increases fourfold.
At a constant degradation rate a twofold production increase predicts about a twofold steady-state amount.
The larger change suggests altered stability or processing in addition to altered synthesis.
Untreated mRNA has a half-life of 2 h.
After two consecutive 2 h intervals with hormone, about 0.71²≈0.50 remains.
Estimated hormone-treated half-life is approximately 4 h.
The data support altered RNA production and decay but do not identify a binding molecule or site.
Measure occupancy of the promoter by the hormone-activated receptor, comparing hormone and control conditions.
Mutate the proposed response sequence in a matched reporter and test whether hormone-dependent activation is lost; accept another relevant causal test.

questions.answerSummary: New RNA doubles while steady-state mature RNA increases fourfold.
